newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-MEXICO HELD TO DRAW BY COSTA RICA BUT ADVANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MEXICO HELD TO DRAW BY COSTA RICA BUT ADVANCE.

text.p: Mexico qualified for the Copa America soccer tournament quarter-finals despite struggling to a 1-1 draw against underdogs Costa Rica on Thursday.
Mexico, again backed by a mariachi band in the stands, were outplayed by their Central American rivals and needed a controversial penalty for their goal in the group C game.
The penalty, awarded for an alleged handball, was converted by Luis Hernandez in the 15th minute for his fifth goal of the competition. It was also the 2,000th goal in the tournament's history.

Costa Rica completely dominated after the goal and created five clearcut chances before halftime against a Mexican team that was a shadow of the side which played so well in Monday's 3-2 defeat by Brazil.
Two efforts were cleared off the line by Mexican defenders, two were well-saved by goalkeeper Adolfo Rios and one was somehow fired wide by Rolando Fonseca from point blank range.
Costa Rica continued to control the game after halftime and deservedly equalised in the 60th minute through striker Hernan Medford.
Medford, a veteran of the country's only World Cup appearance in 1990, picked up the ball, ran at the defence and cut inside to score with a drive from 25 metres.
Mexico finished with four points and, even if they finish third in their group, will advance as one of the two best third-placed teams.
Costa Rica, in their first appearance in the competition, finished bottom with one point despite playing some skilful football.
Hernandez, given hero status after a superb performance against Brazil when he scored two goals, was left isolated up front and was kept under wraps by the Costa Rica defence.
